tonight.headline: Friday cleared everyone — and JuiceJam start DeVonta Smith at 0.0
body: Bad news first: at 12:15 CDMX today Jalen Coker was benched for DK Metcalf. The projection still prefers Coker by 0.6 — a coin flip, but the wrong side of it, and nothing reported since this morning favours Metcalf (card below). Alvin Kamara has no designation for Paris (RotoWire game page) but stays the fourth back behind Kendre Miller; Rico Dowdle is questionable (knee), which can only help Jaylen Warren.

Love, Jefferson, Coker, Gordon, Likely and Wilson all came off Friday's reports without a designation (NFL.com Week 7 report). ESPN now has AVIATO 68%, 130.1 to 95.7: JuiceJam's projection fell because DeVonta Smith (hamstring, did not practise Friday) sits in their lineup at 0.0 for Monday night.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: JuiceJam need Bryce Young (17.8) and CeeDee Lamb (18.5) to beat their numbers while Love and Jefferson miss theirs — and they still have to fix the Smith hole; Addison (10.9, full all week per Vikings.com) sits on their bench.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Sunday-morning inactive among your starters. Every one of them was undesignated on Friday, so nothing is armed; check the 07:30 Paris inactives (Warren, Metcalf) at 06:00 CDMX.

doFirst.title: Put Coker back in the flex over Metcalf
doFirst.subtitle: The projection prefers Coker 15.5 to 14.9 — a coin flip it takes, and Friday gave no news that moves it.

case.label: The call
case.body: lineup_check.py: lineup as set 130.2, projection lineup 130.8. The only difference is Coker over Metcalf in the flex, labelled COIN FLIP. Coin flips go to the projection with no thesis (STRATEGY §1).

case.label: What Friday said
case.body: Coker is not on Carolina's Friday report — everyone but Phillips, Incoom, Freeling and Martin-Scott was a full participant (Panthers.com 23 Oct 12:26). Bryce Young is undesignated. Metcalf is not on Pittsburgh's report either; Skowronek and Echols are out (RotoWire PIT-NO). Both roles are intact; neither side has unpriced news.

case.label: Why it is a card
case.body: The swap was made at 18:15Z today (activity log). If it rests on Metcalf's 15 targets last week, that is volume — the backtest says it made start/sit worse at every weight. If you had a reason I cannot see, keep it: the expected cost is 0.6.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf outscores Coker in Week 7 (archive). A coin flip, so the outcome is noted, not logged as a thesis.

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup moved off the projection at 12:15 today
whatWentWrong.lead: Metcalf in, Coker out — 0.6 below the projection lineup on a coin flip.

case.label: What happened
case.body: This morning the lineup as set was the projection lineup (130.9). At 18:15Z Metcalf went into the flex and Coker to the bench (activity log). No Friday report touched either player.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: In weeks 1-2 the biggest losses came from moving off the projection on last week's points; Metcalf's 15 targets in Week 6 are the same kind of signal. The card above puts it back.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: News surfaces before Sunday 07:30 that ESPN has not priced and that favours Metcalf — a Coker injury or a Carolina quarterback change.

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 11.0 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Kamara's 14.9 sat behind Allgeier's 5.8 and Love's 20.2 behind Allen's 18.3 — both projection calls, neither an override.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 122.6 to 82.94 over Bok-aneers; best possible lineup 133.6 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost. The fix is not to override — it is to set the lineup every week, which is done for Week 7: the lineup as set is the projection lineup.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: A Week 7 lineup set by projection leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).

worthALook.name: Michael Mayer
worthALook.lead: Week 8 tight-end cover — weaker now that Bowers practised in full on Friday.

case.label: The player
case.body: 9 targets, 7 for 95 in Week 6 beside Brock Bowers (Spectrum/AP 18 Oct). Bowers went from limited Wednesday to FULL on Friday with no game status (Raiders.com 23 Oct 13:14), so Mayer is the second tight end again.

case.label: The cost
case.body: A free agent — no claim. Chem starts one tight end and a second has no flex route, so he is a one-week rental for Likely's Week 8 bye.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Next Tuesday on Week 8 projections, dropping a bye-week body. Changes if he draws under 5 targets against the Rams with Bowers active.

worthALook.name: Hunter Henry
worthALook.lead: The other Week 8 tight-end answer: 7 targets on 78% of snaps Thursday.

case.label: The player
case.body: 7 catches for 71 on 7 targets, 78% of snaps and 71% of routes in Thursday's loss at Chicago (RotoWire usage 22 Oct); Eli Raridon took 52% of snaps and scored, so it is a two-tight-end offence.

case.label: The cost
case.body: He is on waivers until Wed 28 Oct 01:00 CDMX — a claim, though Chem's priority resets weekly, so it costs nothing lasting. Mayer is free and costs nothing at all.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Next Tuesday, against Mayer on Week 8 projections, as cover for Likely's Giants bye. Changes if New England's Week 8 matchup or Raridon's share cuts his routes under 60%. Carried from this morning's research; not re-searched this run.

doNotChase.name: Tyler Allgeier
doNotChase.lead: Jeremiyah Love is ruled out again — and it is still a committee Bam Knight won last week.

case.label: The case for
case.body: Love OUT for Week 7 (ankle), Arizona resting him until he is 100% (SI 22 Oct; NFL.com Week 7 report). Allgeier took 56% of snaps and 18 carries in Week 6 and should get the goal line against a Denver defence 7th-most generous to backs (SI 22 Oct; DeepMetric).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 18 carries for 38 yards, 2.1 a carry, against Bam Knight's 15 for 80 on 44% of snaps (SI 22 Oct). SI's own read: a bigger committee than expected, no clear split.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Love placed on IR and Allgeier named the lead — and even then not a reversal of the 21 Oct drop.

doNotChase.sources: SI 22 Oct · NFL.com Week 7 report · DeepMetric

doNotChase.name: Bam Knight
doNotChase.lead: Out-gained Allgeier 80 to 38 — and is still the second back in a split.

case.label: The case for
case.body: 15 carries for 80 yards (5.3 a carry), 2 catches on 44% of snaps in Week 6 with Love out; SI calls him a viable flex with Love out again (SI 22 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 44% of snaps, behind Allgeier's 56% and the goal line; a free agent filling a vacancy that ends when Love returns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Knight out-snaps Allgeier at Denver and Love goes to IR.

doNotChase.name: Roschon Johnson
doNotChase.lead: The week's biggest riser had 2 carries on Thursday — D'Andre Swift took the backfield.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Swift played 86% of snaps and handled 26 of 28 running-back opportunities; Johnson 14% of snaps, 2 carries for 13 (RotoWire usage 22 Oct). The ownership jump was bought on Monangai's injury, and Swift, not Johnson, inherited it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Swift hurt and Monangai (turf toe, uncertain for Week 8 at Seattle per RotoWire) still out — then Johnson is the only back left. Carried from this morning's research (RotoWire TNF usage 22 Oct); not re-searched this run.
